speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry with regard to the upcoming Sungei Kadut Eco-district (a) whether JTC has performed any environmental baseline study (EBS) or environmental impact assessment (EIA) for the development; (b) if so, whether the outcome of the study/assessment can be made public; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider mandating all future similar industrial park developments to have EIA or EBS conducted with public consultations with various stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I will address all of these questions together today.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The former Keretapi Tanah Melayu (KTM) railway line used to run through the Kranji Road/Kranji Close site.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When the KTM land was returned to Singapore in 2011, the said site comprised mainly disused scrubland.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is shown on page 3 of the handout.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As the site was earmarked for future development works, it was left vacant.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: More non-native Albizia trees then sprouted over the years.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In 2015, following the Urban Redevelopment Authority's (URA’s) review of the plans for the KTM land parcels, the Rail Corridor was realigned out of the Kranji parcel so that the site could be redeveloped for industrial use.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The plan was publicly exhibited, and community stakeholders were generally receptive to the proposal.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is shown in page 6 of the handout.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In its development plans for the AFIP, JTC recognised the importance of retaining greenery, and therefore proposed to preserve the original alignment of the former KTM railway line within AFIP as a green corridor with additional green buffers on each side.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: JTC’s development plans for AFIP with the green corridor were publicly exhibited in URA’s Draft Master Plan 2019 and the SKED Master Plan exhibition in February 2020.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I will now go through the development works at the Kranji site.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In response to Ms He Ting Ru’s question, page 9 of the handout provides a background on the roles and responsibilities of the various parties involved in a typical development project, including that of AFIP.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Besides the contractor, an important party is the consultant, who acts as the Qualified Person (QP).

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In particular, the QP is responsible for ensuring that the project’s design meet the statutory requirements, and obtaining approvals from the authorities for the design.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Dennis Tan have asked about the sequence of land clearing activities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: JTC’s chronology has been reported widely in the media, and Members may refer to pages 10 to 15 of the handout for the chronology.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I will therefore just highlight a few key points.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In 2019, JTC appointed CPG as its consultant to carry out planning and design works for the site.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: An Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) was not required then, given that the site was previously dominated by scrubland vegetation and later non-native Albizia trees as I had explained earlier.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The site is also not close to sensitive nature areas.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Thereafter, CPG submitted building plans for AFIP to NParks, including proposals to fell trees.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On 29 August 2019, NParks issued a Written Direction to approve the tree-felling for three plots within the site, namely Plots 4, 5 and 9 indicated on page 11 of the handout.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Following this, tree felling for Plot 9 started in March 2020.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In August 2020, CPG submitted updated building plans to NParks, which included a new drain with discharge and flow into Sungei Pang Sua.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As the drain could potentially cause sediments from the site to flow into Sungei Pang Sua and impact wildlife in the vicinity, NParks instructed JTC and CPG to conduct a fauna baseline study and Environmental Monitoring and Management Programme (EMMP).

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The consultant for the fauna study and EMMP was engaged in December 2020.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These areas are edged red in page 14 of the handout and amount to a total of 4.5 hectares.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There are on-going investigations on why the contractor did so, since there was no approval.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I seek the House’s understanding that I cannot say more at this point in time, pending the outcome of these investigations.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The further land clearing by the contractor was discovered by JTC’s project manager on 13 January 2021 during his site visit.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All clearance works onsite were suspended immediately and remain suspended today.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan and Ms He Ting Ru asked how we will ensure such incidents do not recur.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: JTC has commenced an internal investigation to ascertain what had happened and why.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The investigation will be led by JTC’s Senior Management who are not involved in the project.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It will check if JTC’s current processes for land clearance works were followed by both the public officers and private contractors involved.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: JTC will also review how it can better supervise the various personnel involved in its development projects.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: NParks is separately investigating whether there were breaches to the Parks and Trees Act and the Wildlife Act.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will not comment further on the respective investigations at this point to not prejudice the outcomes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Till today, all clearance works on the Kranji Close/Kranji Road site remain suspended.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: After the fauna baseline study and EMMP are completed around April 2021, JTC will engage key stakeholders, including nature interest groups, to discuss its development plans.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Findings of the studies will be made publicly available when ready.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Minister Desmond Lee and I have also asked Permanent Secretary Joseph Leong, who is not involved in this matter, to lead a review of the lessons arising from this development at Kranji.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In the course of his review, he will consult representatives from the public, private and people sectors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It was scrubland that has become overgrown in recent years.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The project was carefully planned, incorporating and balancing the considerations of economic development, job creation and environmental protection.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The execution of the land clearing could be improved.
